name: Briscolone
description: Briscolone is a two-player trick-taking card game without a trump suit. Players follow suit when possible and use Briscola-style point values to win tricks and accumulate a running total over several deals.

overview.description: Briscolone is a two-player trick-taking card game without a trump suit. Players follow suit when possible and use Briscola-style point values to win tricks and accumulate a running total over several deals.

history.origins:
Country/Region of Origin: Italy
Time Period: Early 20th century
Historical Development: Briscolone evolved as a larger two-player variant of the Italian point-trick game Briscola, using the same card values but dealing more cards and removing the trump suit.
Cultural Significance: Played as a casual head-to-head game and described in modern Italian card-game collections.
timeline: Modern Era: Continues to be played worldwide

scoring.description: Card points won in tricks using standard Briscola values: ace 11, three 10, king 4, queen 3, jack 2, and all other cards worth 0. Each deal contains 120 card points.
scoring.winCondition: Play several deals and add the card points from tricks; the first player to reach the agreed cumulative target (commonly 121 or 151 points) wins the game.

synthesis.shortDescription: Briscolone is a trick-taking card game that involves tricks, trump, following suit. The game originated in Europe and has become popular worldwide.
